title: The maximum G-different permutation conjecture
literal_statement:
A **natural graph** is a simple graph whose vertex set is a finite subset of $\mathbb{N}$. Two infinite permutations of $\mathbb{N}$ are **$G$-different** if, for some coordinate $i\in\mathbb{N}$, the two entries at that coordinate are the endpoints of an edge of $G$. Let $\kappa(G)$ be the maximum cardinality of a set of infinite permutations that are pairwise $G$-different, and define

$$
K(\ell)=\max\{\kappa(G)\;\ |E(G)|=\ell\}.
$$

**The maximum G-different permutation conjecture.** For every $\ell\in\mathbb{N}$,

$$
K(\ell)=3^\ell.
$$

The paper proves that $K(\ell)$ lies between $3^\ell$ and $4^\ell$ for every natural number $\ell$, so the conjectured exact lower endpoint remains unresolved.
full_scope_mechanism_or_obstacle: The lower construction gives 3^ell but a proof needs an upper bound for every graph with ell edges and every family of infinite permutations; optimizing a fixed finite graph misses that quantifier. No uniform compression to 3 choices per edge established.

title: The product replacement graph connectivity conjecture
literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, and let $d(G)$ denote the minimum size of a generating set of $G$. For an integer $k\geq d(G)$, let $\tilde \Gamma_k(G)$ be the extended product replacement algorithm graph whose vertices are the generating $k$-tuples of $G$ and whose edges correspond to Nielsen moves.

**Connectivity conjecture.** If $k\geq d(G)+1$, then $\tilde \Gamma_k(G)$ is connected.

This question was raised by Pak because no examples were known of a finite group $G$ and an integer $k\geq d(G)+1$ for which the extended product replacement graph is disconnected. The conjecture is known for finite abelian and finite solvable groups, and general bounds are known, but it is not established for all finite groups.
full_scope_mechanism_or_obstacle: Nielsen orbit connectivity must hold for every finite group with only one spare generator. The primary bounds d(G)+mu(G) and solvable cases do not close the gap to d(G)+1 for arbitrary nonsolvable groups; park structural group program.

title: Conjecture on the cop number of graphs embedded in non-orientable surfaces
literal_statement:
Let $c(g)$ denote the maximum cop number of a graph embedded in an orientable surface of genus $g$, and let $\tilde c(g)$ denote the corresponding maximum for graphs embedded in a non-orientable surface of genus $g$. **Surface cop-number conjecture.**

$$
\tilde c(g)=c(\lfloor g/2\rfloor).
$$

The preceding argument establishes the upper bound $\tilde c(g)\leq c(g-1)$ using the orientable double cover, while the equality for all genera is presented as a conjecture and its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
full_scope_mechanism_or_obstacle: The orientable double-cover strategy only yields c(g-1). The primary conclusion explicitly says other orientable branched covers factor through that cover, so improving the cover alone cannot establish c(floor(g/2)) for all genera.

title: Unbounded integral point sets over prime residue rings
literal_statement:

$$
\dot{\mathcal{I}}(\mathbb{Z}_p,2)\ge l.
$$

The surrounding discussion notes that several non-isomorphic sets attain the upper bound and suggests only the weaker observation that the value is at least $7$ for sufficiently large primes. Over the integers, the corresponding question for seven points is stated to remain unsolved.

title: Sum-rate conjecture for the binary skew-symmetric broadcast channel
literal_statement:
Let $(U,V)$ be auxiliary random variables and let $X,Y_1,Y_2$ be the input and outputs of the binary skew-symmetric channel with $p=\frac{1}{2}$, such that $(U,V) \to X \to (Y_1,Y_2)$ is a Markov chain. **Sum-rate conjecture.** The following inequality holds:

$$
I(U;Y_1) + I(V;Y_2) - I(U;V) \leq \max\{I(X;Y_1), I(X;Y_2)\}.
$$

If true, this conjecture would bound the sum rate of the Márton inner bound by approximately $0.3616$, while the evaluated outer bound has maximum sum rate approximately $0.3711$. Thus it would establish that the inner and outer bounds are not tight for the binary skew-symmetric channel.

title: The subdivided complete-graph conjecture for the cop number
literal_statement:
Let $K_n$ be a complete graph, and let $G$ be any graph obtained from $K_n$ by subdividing its edges, possibly a non-uniform number of times. The cop number of $G$, denoted by $\operatorname{cop}(G)$, is the minimum number of cops needed to capture a robber on $G$.

title: Conjecture on disjoint duplexes in Latin squares
literal_statement:
A **$k$-plex** in a Latin square of order $n$ is a set of entries containing each row, column, and symbol exactly $k$ times. A **duplex** is a $2$-plex, and a **$k$-partition** is a partition of the Latin square into disjoint $k$-plexes.

**Duplex partition conjecture.** Every Latin square has the maximum possible number of disjoint duplexes. In particular, every Latin square of even order has a $2$-partition, and every Latin square of odd order has a $(2,2,2,\dots,2,1)$-partition.

The conjecture strengthens Ryser's conjecture and implies the existence of $k$-plexes for every even $k$ up to the order of the square. It is known for Latin squares of orders at most $8$ and for soluble groups, but remains open in general.
full_scope_mechanism_or_obstacle: Need disjoint 2-plexes exhausting every even-order square, or leaving one transversal for odd order. Finding a single duplex does not iterate through a Latin square after removal; odd case includes Ryser. Source soluble-group cases do not cover all squares.

title: The spectral gap conjecture for multi-species ASEP
literal_statement:
Let $m=(m_1,\,\ldots,m_n)\in\mathcal M$ be a sector, let ${\rm Spec}(m)$ denote the spectrum in that sector, and let $E_j^{\pm}(m)=E^{\pm}(m_1+\cdots+m_j,m_{j+1}+\cdots+m_n)$ for $1\leq j\leq n-1$, where $E^{\pm}$ are the second largest eigenvalues in the corresponding one-species sectors. **Spectral gap conjecture.** In any sector $m=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)\in\mathcal M$, there is no eigenvalue $E\in{\rm Spec}(m)$ such that

$$
\max\{{\rm Re}\,E^{\pm}_1(m),\ldots,{\rm Re}\,E^{\pm}_{n-1}(m)\}< {\rm Re}\,E<0.
$$

The one-species case $n=2$ is immediate from the definition, and the conjecture had been checked in all sectors with $\dim V(m)<8000$; its general validity remains open.

title: Finite-translate perfect-squares conjecture
literal_statement:
Let $\textsc{Squares}$ denote the set of perfect squares in $\mathbb Z$. **Finite-translate perfect-squares conjecture.** There exists a positive integer $k$ such that there are no sets $X,Y\subset\mathbb Z$ with $|X|=|Y|=k$ satisfying

$$
x+y\in\textsc{Squares}\quad\text{for all }x\in X\text{ and }y\in Y.
$$

This asks whether the maximum number of translates of a fixed-size set of integers into the perfect squares is finite for some size. Such a bound would have consequences for sum-product exponents on sparse graphs; the problem is stated as open.

title: Rational generating-function conjecture for maximum independent sets of de Bruijn graphs
literal_statement:
For a positive integer $d$ and a fixed diameter $D$, let $B(d,D)$ be the de Bruijn graph and let $a_{d,D}$ denote the number of maximum independent sets of $B(d,D)$. Consider its exponential generating function

$$
\sum_{d=1}^{\infty}\frac{a_{d,D}t^d}{d!}.
$$

**Rational generating-function conjecture.** If $D$ is a fixed odd prime number, then this exponential generating function is the ratio of two polynomials, each of degree $D-1$.
For $D=3$, the paper proves the analogous assertion with numerator and denominator of degree at most $2$; the conjecture proposes the stated degree bound for every fixed odd prime diameter.
full_scope_mechanism_or_obstacle: Need orbit classification or alphabet-extension recurrence for every odd prime D, not just D=3. Primary discussion explicitly requires new extension functions for all increments below D; computing coefficients cannot prove the rational EGF degree bound.

title: The arbitrary-target distribution conjecture for pebbling
literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let $t$ be a positive integer. Define $\pi(G,t)$ to be the smallest number of pebbles such that every target distribution of size $t$ is reachable from every distribution of at least that size, and let $\pi_t(G)$ be the $t$-pebbling number.

**Arbitrary-target distribution conjecture.**

$$
\pi(G,t)=\pi_t(G).

title: Continuous Hirsch conjecture
literal_statement:
For a polytope $P$ of dimension $d$ defined by $n$ inequalities and a linear objective function $c$, let $\lambda_c(P)$ be the total curvature of its central path. Let $\Lambda(n,d)$ be the largest such total curvature over all such $P$ and $c$. **Continuous Hirsch conjecture.** There is a constant $K$ such that

$$
\Lambda(n,d)\leq Kn
$$

for all $n$ and $d$, equivalently $\Lambda(n,d)\in O(n)$. The previously proposed constant and linear-in-dimension bounds for central-path curvature were disproved by constructions showing exponential growth in $d$ and, for fixed $d\geq 2$, $\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Lambda(n,d)/n\geq\pi$.

title: Prime-depleted Szpiro conjecture for elliptic curves
literal_statement:
Let $K$ be a number field. For an integral ideal $\mathfrak{D}=\prod_i\mathfrak{p}_i^{e_i}$, let $\sigma_J(\mathfrak{D})$ be the minimum of the Szpiro ratios obtained after removing up to $J$ of its prime-power factors. In particular, $\mathfrak{D}(E/K)$ denotes the discriminant ideal of an elliptic curve $E/K$.

**Prime-depleted Szpiro conjecture.** There exist an integer $J\ge0$ and a constant $C_3$, depending only on $K$, such that for all elliptic curves $E/K$,

$$
\sigma_J\bigl(\mathfrak{D}(E/K)\bigr)\le C_3.
$$

This weakens the classical Szpiro conjecture because increasing $J$ can only decrease the depleted Szpiro ratio. The paper introduces this conjecture as the key hypothesis used to obtain Lang's height conjecture.
full_scope_mechanism_or_obstacle: Deleting a bounded number of discriminant prime factors still leaves a uniform height/discriminant problem over all elliptic curves. No bounded-height enumeration controls J and C for an entire number field; source relates it to prime-depleted ABC, so park arithmetic program.

title: Chudnovsky–Seymour–Sullivan conjecture on cycles in triangle-free digraphs
literal_statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple digraph with no directed cycle of length at most three; call such a digraph **3-free**. Let $\beta(G)$ be the minimum cardinality of a set $X\subseteq E(G)$ such that $G\setminus X$ is acyclic, and let $gamma(G)$ be the number of unordered pairs of nonadjacent vertices of $G$.

**Chudnovsky–Seymour–Sullivan conjecture.** If $G$ is a 3-free digraph, then

$$
\beta(G) \leq \frac{1}{2}\gamma(G).
$$

Chudnovsky, Seymour, and Sullivan proved the weaker bound $\beta(G)\leq\gamma(G)$, later improved by Dunkum, Hamburger, and Pór to $\beta(G)\leq 0.88\gamma(G)$; the conjectured factor $1/2$ remains unresolved in the source.

title: Core semisparsity conjecture for quotient representations of polytopes
literal_statement:
Let $W$ be a group and let $N$ be a subgroup of $W$. The subgroup $N$ is **semisparse** in $W$ if it satisfies the semisparsity condition for quotient representations, and let $\operatorname{Core}(W,N)$ denote the core of $N$ in $W$, namely the largest normal subgroup of $W$ contained in $N$.

**Core semisparsity conjecture.** If $N$ is semisparse in $W$, then $\operatorname{Core}(W,N)$ is also semisparse.

A positive answer would imply that the two open questions described in the paper have negative answers: every finite polytope would have a well-defined quotient construction using the core, and every finite polytope would admit a presentation as a quotient of a finite regular polytope. The source does not report a resolution of this conjecture.

Need exact distinguished-generator/intersection conditions and a finite regular-cover theorem; the source finite group search cannot prove core semisparsity for all W.

title: Half-degree conjecture for complementary tuples in balanced multipartite hypergraphs
literal_statement:
Let $H$) be an $n$-balanced $r$-partite $r$-graph, and let $I$ be a subset of $[r]:=\{1,2,\ldots,r\}$. An **$I$-tuple** is an element of $\times_{i\in I}V_i$, and write $I^c:=[r]\setminus I$. For an $I$-tuple $f$ and an $I^c$-tuple $g$, let $d(f)$ and $d(g)$ denote their degrees in $H$. **Half-degree conjecture.** If

$$
d(f)>\frac{n^{r-|I|}}{2}
$$

for every $I$-tuple $f$ and

$$
d(g)\geq\frac{n^{|I|}}{2}
$$

for every $I^c$-tuple $g$, then $H$ has a perfect matching. Thus, each tuple has degree at least roughly half of its possible degree, with a strict inequality on the $I$-side. The condition would weaken the sharp minimum-degree hypothesis proved earlier in the paper; its general validity is presented as an open problem.
full_scope_mechanism_or_obstacle: The two complementary tuple-degree inequalities give density and fractional matching information, but an integral perfect matching must avoid conflicts in every part simultaneously. Hall on a graph of tuples does not ensure coordinate-disjointness; source fractional theorem is not the required integral result.

title: The superlinear blocker conjecture with bounded collinearities

For fixed $\ell$, let $b_\ell(n)$ be the minimum integer such that every set of $n$ points in the plane with no $\ell$ collinear points can be blocked by a set of $b_\ell(n)$ points. **Bounded-collinearity blocker conjecture.** For all fixed $\ell$,

$$
\frac{b_\ell(n)}{n}\rightarrow\infty\quad\text{as }n\rightarrow\infty.
$$

This generalizes the general-position case $b_3(n)=b(n)$ and is stated in the source as implying the Big-Line-Big-Chromatic-Number Conjecture; its general status remains open.
full_scope_mechanism_or_obstacle: Record uses every point set whereas blocking-number minima in the source need quantifier reconciliation. Midpoint superlinearity does not transfer: arbitrary blockers can lie at unequal ratios. An all-configuration incidence bound with fixed collinearity cap is still needed.

title: Conjecture that random graphs of fixed genus are asymptotically almost surely 4-chromatic
literal_statement:
Let $g$ be fixed, and let $G_n$ be a graph chosen uniformly at random from the graphs of genus $g$ with $n$ vertices. The chromatic number of $G_n$ is the minimum number of colors needed to color its vertices so that adjacent vertices receive different colors.

**Chromatic-number conjecture.** The chromatic number of a random graph of fixed genus $g$ with $n$ vertices is asymptotically almost surely equal to $4$.

The preceding theorem establishes that the chromatic number is asymptotically almost surely either $4$ or $5$; the conjecture asserts that the value $4$ occurs with probability tending to $1$.

Linear K4 copies prove the lower bound 4 and large facewidth gives 5-colorability, but neither eliminates global 5-color obstructions; enumeration needs uniform asymptotic control.

title: Superlinear blocker-number conjecture
literal_statement:

$$
\frac{b(n)}{n}\rightarrow\infty\quad\text{as }n\rightarrow\infty.
$$

title: The complete extremal-family conjecture for maximal-chain traces
literal_statement:
Let $W(n,k,r)$ denote the maximum size of a family $\mathcal{A}\subset [n]^{(k)}$ whose trace on every $r$-subset of $[n]$ contains no maximal chain. **The complete extremal-family conjecture.** For $r\geq 2$, if $k+r-1\leq n<2k$, then

$$
W(n,k,r)=\binom{k+r-1}{k},
$$

and the only extremal family is of the form $[k+r-1]^{(k)}$; if $n>2k$, then

$$
W(n,k,r)=\binom{n-k+r-1}{r-1},
$$

and the only extremal family is of the form $\{A\in[n]^{(k)}:1,2,\ldots,k-r+1\in A\}$. This proposes the extremal numbers and equality cases for all indicated ranges of $n$, complementing the large-$n$ results proved earlier in the paper; the source supplies no resolution status for the full assertion.
full_scope_mechanism_or_obstacle: Both ranges demand sharp size and uniqueness of equality families, including near n=2k. Large-n compression bounds do not yield the exact threshold or equality classification; missing k>=r conventions are a scope check, not a new result.

title: Meta-isomorphism conjecture for assembly maps
literal_statement:
Fix a group $G$, a family of subgroups $\mathcal{F}$, and a $G$-homology theory $\mathcal{H}^G_*$. Let $E_{\mathcal{F}}(G)$ be the classifying $G$-space for the family $\mathcal{F}$, and let

$$
A_{\mathcal{F}}\colon\mathcal{H}^G_n(E_{\mathcal{F}}(G))\to\mathcal{H}^G_n(\operatorname{pt})
$$

be the assembly map induced by the projection $E_{\mathcal{F}}(G)\to\operatorname{pt}$.

**Meta-isomorphism conjecture.** The assembly map $A_{\mathcal{F}}$ is an isomorphism for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}$.

The source notes that the assertion is automatic for the family of all subgroups; the content is to choose the smallest possible family for which it remains true. Farrell–Jones and Baum–Connes conjectures are presented as instances.

title: Non-finite generation conjecture for the cohomology of Johnson filtration subgroups
literal_statement:
Let $F_n$ be the free group of rank $n$, let $\Gamma^{s+1}$ be the $(s+1)$st term of its lower central series, and let $J_n^s$ denote the kernel of the homomorphism

$$
\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)\to \operatorname{Aut}(F_n/\Gamma^{s+1}).
$$

For integers $n$, $s$, and $i$ satisfying $3\leq n$, $2\leq s$, and $1\leq i\leq n-2$, **the authors' weak conjecture.** The cohomology group $H^i(J_n^s)$ is not finitely generated.

The preceding results give rapidly growing ranks for related cohomology groups and construct classes in the indicated degrees, but do not establish finite-generation failure for all these parameters. The conjecture remains open in the source.
full_scope_mechanism_or_obstacle: Rapidly growing finite ranks of related groups do not imply a fixed H^i(J_n^s) is infinitely generated. Need infinitely many independent classes surviving in that one subgroup in each indicated degree; source Johnson images give finite-rank information only.
